object_description: linear two-story school volume with a loggia-like park frontage
design_condition: The building is placed at the park edge as a linear body, with terrain modulation and a lowered northern development preserving panoramic views while creating varied public and protected outdoor spaces.

positive.statement: The park creates an atmospherically varied and easily usable neighborhood open space.

position.rationale: The open park-edge zone is approximated along the southern side of the elongated school volume.

positive.statement: The clear, pleasantly restrained design brings the park, stream, school and existing farm together into a convincing whole.

position.target: park, stream, school and existing farm
position.rationale: The surrounding landscape relationship is anchored outside the building's southern park frontage.

positive.statement: The outward-facing access gives the school a strong public message as a meeting place.

position.rationale: The long public-facing edge is visible along the park-facing side of the linear volume.

positive.statement: The sectional solution preserves the panoramic view of the park.

position.rationale: The park-facing upper edge provides the plausible viewpoint anchor for preserved views.

positive.statement: The location and accessibility of the multi-purpose room and sports changing rooms enable external use without disrupting school operations.

position.target: multi-purpose room and sports changing rooms
position.rationale: External-use rooms are approximated near the park-facing end of the elongated school.

positive.statement: The stringency of the internal organization affects the clarity of the external expression.

position.rationale: The linear building mass anchors the internal organization, which is not directly resolved.

positive.statement: The serial timber construction logic creates a robust appearance appropriate to the location and school level.

position.rationale: Repeated longitudinal facade lines and stacked levels support a robust serial construction reading.

positive.statement: The proposal promises very good economic and ecological values through flexibility and compactness.

position.rationale: The statement evaluates performance rather than a specific spatial location.

positive.statement: The project impresses with surprising simplicity, directness and robustness.

position.rationale: The simple elongated mass and consistent levels provide a whole-building anchor.

positive.statement: Its expansion in the flow direction of the park creates a strong identity.

position.rationale: The linear footprint visibly extends diagonally along the park-edge direction.

negative.statement: The many path connections on the access street are not convincing.

position.rationale: Street connections are approximated along the park-facing southern access edge.

negative.statement: The gently sloping gable roof is not yet convincing as a fifth facade.

position.rationale: The elongated roof outline is clearly visible above the two-story linear volume.

negative.statement: The arrangement requires greater attention to the use of daylight.

position.rationale: Daylight is internal, so the building envelope provides a constrained placement.

negative.statement: The highly installed ventilation concept would have to be re-examined together with the sponsor.

position.rationale: The ventilation system is not visible; it is approximated within the building envelope.

negative.statement: The investment costs are slightly above the target construction costs for the school sector.

position.rationale: The statement concerns project cost without a spatial referent.
